about: Riesling is the grape the Finger Lakes are best known for, and Dr. Konstantin Frank was among the first to prove it could survive here. The Ukrainian-born scientist planted vinifera on Keuka Lake in 1958 and opened his winery in 1962. Margrit is one of the family’s HELM wines, which honor the women of Dr. Frank. It is a tribute to Margrit Frank, who gave much of herself to the winery’s growth and to the people around her, and whose sunny, welcoming nature inspired the wine.

Margrit comes from a single plot on the family’s Seneca Lake estate in Hector, planted in 2012 at about 940 feet in deep Honeoye gravelly silt loam. The site sits in the “Banana Belt,” a mesoclimate a few degrees warmer than Keuka, and is NY Sustainable Winegrowing certified. The 2024 was picked on October 11 after an early, warm season and a cool, sunny autumn, then destemmed, pressed directly and fermented cool in stainless steel with no malolactic fermentation and no oak.

The winery describes lime zest, apricot, ripe melon and tropical florals over a shale and mineral core, with bright acidity, a creamy texture, stone fruit and crunchy minerality on the palate and a long, elegant finish. James Suckling rated the 2024 92 points. Only 322 cases were made, so it is one of the smaller Rieslings in a cellar known for the grape, and a good look at what the warmer Seneca side of the family’s vineyards can do.
